theme: Earnings-call transcript datasets and NLP tooling (ECT datasets, Motley Fool scrapers, Seeking Alpha parsers), management-tone corpora

candidates.name: EarningsCall_Dataset (Qin & Yang, ACL 2019)
candidates.what_it_holds: Segmented earnings-call text + aligned audio for S&P 500 companies, ~2017 (e.g. 3M, Amazon, Twitter, Feb-Apr 2017). Folders named CompanyName_Date; text files hold CEO statements split sentence-by-sentence, audio files named Speaker_Paragraph_Sentence. Repo has a handful of example folders + a link to the full set as 5 split zip files on Google Drive (too large for GitHub). 24 commits, no explicit license. Built for the ACL 2019 volatility-prediction paper.
candidates.why_useful: Multimodal (text+audio) earnings-call corpus with a documented sentence-level structure; a template for building/verifying a similar ABNB-specific tone corpus and a source of peer (S&P 500) call data for cross-sectional tone/volatility benchmarking.
candidates.time_coverage: 2017 (sample folders); full set scope not independently confirmed
candidates.size_hint: few example folders in-repo; full corpus in 5 Google Drive zips (size unstated)
candidates.last_activity: 24 commits on master, exact date not surfaced

candidates.name: MAEC dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Multimodal Aligned Earnings Conference call corpus, S&P 1500 companies, described as 6x larger than prior academic sets. In-repo: transcripts + low-level audio (CSV) features, 147.7MB, organized YearMonthDay_CompanyCode/text.txt+features.csv. High-level MFCC features (59GB, .npy) hosted on Google Drive. Includes forced-alignment Python code (Python 3.5, pydub/aeneas/ffmpeg). CIKM 2020 paper; CC-BY-SA-4.0 license; 107 stars, 25 forks, 17 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Largest open academic multimodal earnings-call corpus (S&P 1500) with a permissive share-alike license; usable both as a peer-tone benchmark and as a worked example of a text+audio alignment pipeline that could, in principle, be pointed at ABNB's own call audio/transcripts.
candidates.size_hint: 147.7MB in-repo text+CSV features; 59GB audio features via Google Drive
candidates.last_activity: 17 commits, exact date not surfaced; 107 stars

candidates.name: ECTSum (Earnings Call Transcript Summarization, EMNLP 2022)
candidates.what_it_holds: Benchmark dataset pairing earnings-call transcripts with concise bullet-point summaries (from Reuters-style analyst wrap-ups), plus the ECT-BPS extractive+paraphrasing baseline code and processed data files under codes/ECT-BPS/*/data/. GPL-3.0 license, 88 commits, last update 8 Mar 2023 (Colab notebook for the paraphrasing module).
candidates.why_useful: Gives transcript-to-summary training pairs that could be repurposed as a proxy for 'what the sell-side extracted as the key guide items' from a call — directly relevant to modelling what management's guide is made of.
candidates.size_hint: not stated; benchmark-scale (thousands of call/summary pairs typical for this task)

candidates.name: Earnings21 / Earnings22 (Rev.com ASR earnings-call speech datasets)
candidates.what_it_holds: Earnings21: 44 audio files (~39 hours) of 2020 earnings calls with transcripts, speaker labels, punctuation and entity tags. Earnings22: 125 files (~119 hours) of international earnings calls with transcripts, ticker symbols, HQ country and language-region metadata. Distributed via Git LFS; license not explicitly stated in the fetched README.
candidates.why_useful: Real, long-form earnings-call audio+transcript data (not just US large-cap) with entity/ticker metadata; useful as raw material for a from-scratch ABNB peer-call tone/ASR pipeline or for validating a transcript-sourcing method against ground-truth audio.
candidates.time_coverage: Earnings21: 2020 calls; Earnings22: not stated precisely
candidates.size_hint: Earnings21 ~39 hrs/44 files; Earnings22 ~119 hrs/125 files (Git LFS)

candidates.name: defeatbeta-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source Python alternative to Yahoo Finance APIs, backed by DuckDB queries over Hugging Face-hosted datasets (defeat-beta org). Provides valuation ratios, profitability metrics, SEC filings, EARNINGS CALL TRANSCRIPTS, and news, with optional LLM-based call analysis and an MCP server/Claude skill integration. Apache-2.0, 747 stars, 60 forks, 914 commits, actively maintained (Windows needs WSL/Docker).
candidates.why_useful: A live, no-API-key, one-command pull for earnings-call transcripts (and financials) across broad ticker coverage via DuckDB over a Hugging Face dataset — a candidate machine-pullable ABNB (and peer BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT) transcript source that is actively maintained, unlike most one-off scrapers.
candidates.geography: US-listed equities (broad coverage, exact ticker count not confirmed)
candidates.time_coverage: not confirmed; appears to track available filings/transcripts historically
candidates.size_hint: hosted as Hugging Face dataset(s) queried via DuckDB; size not stated
candidates.last_activity: 914 commits on main, actively maintained as of search date

candidates.name: earningscall-python (EarningsCall API client)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for the (freemium/paid) EarningsCall API: transcripts at multiple detail levels (through word-level timestamps), audio downloads, slide decks, speaker/prepared-remarks-vs-Q&A tagging, and an earnings-event calendar; claims 5,000+ companies with an API key. MIT license, Python 3.10+, actively maintained (v2.0.1, 11 Mar 2026), CI via GitHub Actions.
candidates.why_useful: A structured, speaker-tagged, timestamped transcript API client (with a free tier for some data) that could shortcut point-in-time transcript acquisition for ABNB and peers, including audio/slide alignment for tone work.
candidates.size_hint: API client, not a static dataset; 5,000+ companies claimed

candidates.name: motley-fool-earning-transcripts (Datasette)
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js scraper (index.mjs) with a GitHub Actions cron job that scrapes fool.com earnings-call transcripts into a Prisma-managed SQLite DB, served publicly via Datasette at motley-fool-earning-transcripts.fly.dev. 24 commits, no stated license; author disclaims commercial use.
candidates.why_useful: A running, automated, queryable (SQL via Datasette) mirror of Motley Fool transcripts — potentially a faster point-in-time source than re-scraping fool.com directly, though it is itself a scrape of a site with anti-scraping terms (flag as method only, per project rule 6).
candidates.time_coverage: ongoing via cron, start date not stated
candidates.size_hint: SQLite DB served via Datasette; row count not stated
candidates.last_activity: 24 commits, cron-based scraping badge shown as active

candidates.name: motley-fool-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium/webdriver-manager Python scraper (Python 3.7+) for Motley Fool earnings transcripts, built as a 2022 FAU web-scraping workshop exercise. BSD-2-Clause license, 10 commits, last updated Dec 2022. No committed sample data. README explicitly notes fool.com's Terms of Use prohibit scraping and warns not to abuse it.
candidates.why_useful: A minimal, permissively-licensed reference scraper pattern for Motley Fool transcripts; useful only as a documented method, not to be run, since fool.com ToS forbids scraping (a human ToS call per project rule 6).

candidates.name: Earnings-Calls-Transcript-Scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium+BeautifulSoup Python scraper that takes a ticker, finds Motley Fool transcript links, and returns a dict of {date, url, transcript text}. Includes a demo Jupyter notebook, no committed transcript data, 5 commits, last updated Sept 2025, no stated license.
candidates.why_useful: A recently-touched (Sept 2025) Motley Fool scraper pattern, more current than the 2022/2023 alternatives, but again a fool.com scrape — method only, ToS decision deferred to a human per project rule 6.

candidates.name: Motley-Fool-Transcript-Extractor
candidates.what_it_holds: HTML-based personal project to extract Motley Fool articles/transcripts; 0 stars, last updated Feb 2020, no stated license.
candidates.why_useful: Old, low-activity fool.com scraper; catalogued for completeness only, low marginal value versus the other three fool.com scraper hits.

candidates.name: seeking-alpha-scraper-examples
candidates.what_it_holds: github.com/bondvit/seeking-alpha-scraper-examples: runnable Python/JS example calls against a paid Apify 'Seeking Alpha Scraper' actor (valuation, quant ratings, analyst ratings, stock data). 0 stars, last updated 12 Jun 2026. No transcript data committed; requires the paid Apify actor.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Seeking Alpha transcript/data access is effectively paywalled behind a commercial scraping service (Apify) rather than freely available on GitHub; useful mainly as a negative result for the theme.

candidates.name: IBM earnings_call dataset (Lelli et al., DataverseNL)
candidates.what_it_holds: 21,887 rows / 21.1MB: 188 earnings-call transcripts (Thomson Reuters Eikon) for 11 NASDAQ companies, 2016-2020, joined with ~13,200 daily stock-price rows (Yahoo Finance: OHLCV + adjusted close) and sentiment annotations across three subsets. CC0-1.0 (public domain). Originates from a DataverseNL deposit (point of contact Francesco Lelli) and is mirrored on Hugging Face; no primary GitHub repo found.
candidates.why_useful: A small but clean, public-domain, transcript+price-linked dataset with an explicit build methodology (Eikon transcripts joined to daily prices) — a template for building a similar ABNB+peers panel, and CC0 licensing removes reuse friction.

candidates.name: lamini-earnings-calls
candidates.what_it_holds: Archived (13 Jun 2024, read-only) repo with earnings-call transcripts in JSONL (examples include Bilibili/BILI, GFF, at least Q2-Q3 2020), plus the full open-source pipeline used to generate an 860,164-row question-answer dataset from those transcripts (mirrored at huggingface.co/datasets/lamini/earnings-calls-qa, cc-by-4.0). 43 stars, 3 forks, 13 commits, license not stated in-repo but the derived HF dataset is CC-BY-4.0.
candidates.why_useful: A working, reproducible transcript-to-QA generation pipeline plus committed sample transcript JSONL across a range of tickers (semiconductor/tech-heavy in the QA set) — directly reusable code for turning any newly-sourced ABNB/peer transcripts into a structured QA/tone dataset.
candidates.geography: mixed (examples include non-US e.g. Bilibili; QA dataset skews semiconductor/tech: TSMC, Qualcomm, Marvell, Coherent)
candidates.size_hint: derived QA set: 860,164 rows; raw JSONL transcript sample size not stated
candidates.license: not stated in repo; derived HF dataset CC-BY-4.0

candidates.name: FinBERT (Yang, UcHRoy, Huang) — finance-domain BERT incl. earnings-call pretraining
candidates.what_it_holds: Pretrained BERT for financial text, trained on 4.9B tokens: 10-K/10-Q corporate reports (2.5B tokens), EARNINGS CALL TRANSCRIPTS (1.3B tokens), and analyst reports (1.1B tokens); the released finbert-tone variant is fine-tuned on 10,000 manually labeled (pos/neg/neutral) analyst-report sentences. Apache-2.0, 661 stars, 144 forks. Model weights hosted on Hugging Face (yiyanghkust/finbert-tone), including ESG and forward-looking-statement variants.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made, earnings-call-trained tone/sentiment scorer (not a raw ABNB dataset, but a validated tool) that could score ABNB's own and peer transcripts for management-tone features feeding the guide-composition model, without needing to build a tone classifier from scratch.
candidates.size_hint: 4.9B token pretraining corpus (not redistributed raw); 10k labeled sentences for fine-tuning
candidates.last_activity: not stated precisely; multiple HF model variants released
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: team already tested 'management tone' and found it did not beat naive on our construction; this is a different, earnings-call-pretrained tone tool worth trying before concluding tone is dead

candidates.name: edgar-crawler / EDGAR-CORPUS
candidates.what_it_holds: Toolkit to bulk-download and JSON-parse SEC 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K filings for any US-listed company (by CIK/ticker, configurable year/quarter range), plus the pre-built EDGAR-CORPUS (6B+ tokens from annual reports) hosted on Hugging Face and Zenodo. GPLv3, 545 stars, 136 forks, 95 commits, WWW 2025 paper.
candidates.why_useful: Off-theme for pure earnings-call transcripts but directly serves gap #15 (SEC EDGAR full-text/XBRL tooling) and can pull ABNB's own and peers' 8-Ks/10-Qs (guidance language, MD&A) as a companion text corpus to call transcripts for a combined management-language dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: configurable, default 2023; full EDGAR-CORPUS covers many years of annual reports
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: team already holds all ABNB letters/transcripts/XBRL since IPO; this is a general-purpose puller, useful mainly for peer-company text at scale

notes: This session's WebSearch tool was already exhausted (200/200 used, apparently a shared session budget across concurrent scouts) before I ran a single query, so this scout is 100% WebFetch-based: GitHub topics pages, github.com/search (which itself started 429-rate-limiting after ~6 uses), PyPI package pages (good for resolving a tool's real GitHub owner/repo), and Hugging Face dataset pages (good for finding companion GitHub pipeline repos). Dead ends: MiMIC (Indian, single-company, NC license, no GitHub), Seeking Alpha data is effectively paywalled behind a commercial Apify actor with no free GitHub dataset found, and stockanalysis.com has no GitHub scraper presence. Ideas for other scouts: (1) a dedicated pass on Hugging Face 'datasets' search (not just GitHub) surfaced several transcript-derived QA/summary sets in minutes and would likely pay off for other themes too, given how much financial-text tooling now lives there instead of raw GitHub data files; (2) PyPI project pages are a fast way to resolve a package's canonical GitHub org when github.com/search is rate-limited or a guessed owner 404s; (3) worth a follow-up scout specifically on 'IBES/analyst-estimate history' and 'guidance-change' datasets, which came up empty here but are adjacent to gap #4 (point-in-time consensus vintages).
